text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Rules for housing subsidies must be relaxed again as cutbacks have hurt people too much, a parliamentary committee has concluded. It will propose that the government revoke the harshest cutbacks.

- Norwegian companies continue to acquire operations in Sweden to get into the market and to get accesss to new and advanced techniques. In 1995, Norwegian companies invested more than six billion Norwegian crowns in the Swedish business sector, while Swedish companies invested four billion crowns in Norwegian acquisitions.
- Sweden's former tennis star Bjorn Borg might be out of debt soon as some people are prepared to pay part of the debts incurred when his clothing company went bankrupt in 1989.
- Volvo's truck division in the United States has taken 4,500 orders for its new VN series and hopes for an overall upturn in U.S. truck sales.
- Swedish firms taken over by Norwegians say their new owners are too nationalistic and many of their executives are young and lacking international business experience.
- Swedish companies are poor at forecasting European economic trends. Companies last year only reported an upturn in European demand a year after the German IFO index began to rise.
- The government is having trouble finding a buyer for its 25 percent stake in computer consultancy Enator. Potential buyers say that at 6.3 billion crowns it is overpriced by at least 20 percent.
- Deputy Riksbank governor Stefan Ingves favours a merger between the Stockholm Stock Exchange and the OM futures and options exchange.
- Electronic labelling firm Pricer AB is to buy U.S. firm Intactix International Inc for $67 million, to be financed by a two million share new Pricer issue.
